answers.value:
[80] Again missed the fun on higher bands and by the time I got on air the party was almost over, still managed few QSOs. Conditions seemed OK most of stations I worked were at or just above the noise floor at my QTH, meaning their signals were quite strong ( S7 or better ) still hard to copy. Strangely reports I was getting from southern stations were  meager S3 or S5. Normally I do better. SWR looked  OK and my wires were still up so it was fickle propagation again. QSO with vk2vca was our firs contact so I hope to hear Dylan again with a stronger signal for a decant chat. The same with Chris vk1ct, signal below my noise so may be better next time. Last QSO on 80 m was with vk6kd initially signing /4. I got excited assuming he was heading my way. He gave me his QTH as Tilpa which I never heard of before. To my query where it was in QLD he responded with "450 km north west of Brocken Hill" and corrected his signing as /2 so he was well and truly in NSW! I had a quick look at Google Earth and found Tilpa, a tiny place half way between Wilcannia and Bourke, could not be more remote! Well David was unfortunately swinging south-west towards Canberra hoping to catch up with vk2ki. Brisbane visit perhaps in future.
[160] Can not complain three weeks in a raw I am managing at least one QSO on 160 m. This time the culprit was Rob vk3ech, not strong at my QTH but readable ( noise here on 160 is S9 by S-meter ). He gave me RST of 559 quite respectable and I could see both of us at  Ironstone as solid green spackled with red indicating good signals. Unfortunately no other signals just the two of us. I am hoping I am not running out of people with antennas for 160m  so I will continue to call after 10:00 UTC on 1825 KHz any time I make it home early.
A late start on 40m due to fixing the Northeast Beverage. Not enough hours in the day!

This was a busy schedule for the DXperiment project this week, with a lot of FB DX QSOs. Thanks to all stations joining us and sending some beeps around the globe. Very appreciated. Its always a big fun to hear you :-) Have a great week, Mike

On 20m during our QSO with OM Ross, he kept calling me Dave, because conditions were not the best, I repeated  name Manny a few times but I am not sure if he finally got it. I did not hear any David in frequency.
CT7BQF@20, DJ9FM@20, R2VQ@20, SM7CBS@20, UD7M@20, VK2IO@20, VK2KI@20, VK3ACU@20, VK3XU@20, VK6NW@20, VK7TA@20, VK7TO@20,

Thanks, Stan and Greg, for the contacts tonight. Stan, sorry, conditions were not so good on my end, and I had to cut short.

On another front: I have not made any 40m band contacts in the past few weeks. We're heading into the solar minimum, and we'll need to get used to it. Thank you to the last solar maxima. It was great while you were around, and I look forward to the next cycle! EDIT: OK made 1 contact at 40m to VK2 but QSB is so bad I could barely hear him towards the end.

I didn't get home from work until very late on Monday night so missed my sked with my practice sked, so I decided to work from home Tuesday and knocked off in time to catch the afternoon session(s). As it turns out it was a great decision. 

Signals are much stronger here in the late afternoon compared to the evenings and not only did I hear some cracking signals on 40m I even heard DL3YZ with a nice 559 signal, sadly he could not hear me. Other stations heard on 20m were VK7TA, VK3DRQ & VK2IOW.

I cant wait until my time is my own and I can participate more often during the afternoons.

Cheers
Adam VK4IM

After a record setting day of rain (60mm within 24 hours at this QTH) the sky cleared on Tuesday evening with quite good conditions on 80.  After the Boat Anchor Net, using a veteran linear with two 813s, Stan was heard S5 from ZL then nice to catch up with Ketut and OM Manny.
Good conditions on 40m and my ft101e did a fine job cw.
Carnaxide NR. Lisbon Portugal Grid IM58jr

[20m]
Hello everyone,
Once again my little radio managed to reach Australia!!

Thanks Drew VK3XU for the great QSO.

Initially the communication was great, but near the end a QSB started and communication became a bit difficult, but we managed to finish.
Afterwards I called a lot of CQ but didn't get any response, I think the propagation stopped completely.
However, this QSO made my day.

Have a great week everyone.
Thank you 73 Carlos CT7BPF

I answered John VK3BSE CQ call and we had a good time tapping away on our old keys. He was using his AWA Manipulator. Someone came in over the top of us for a while, but we got through that okay. I probably sent a few too many dit dit dit dit dits, but we manage to have a good QSO that seemed to take very little time but was just on an hour.

The Ionosphere certainly excelled itself this week! Pat VK2IOW was S9 - so strong that he could have been in the field next to mine! Mark VK2KI and Jordan VK3ACU had good signals too. David VK2DRQ was, strangely, quieter than usual and surrounded by Snap, Crackles and Pops. Jordan and David demonstrated that you don't have to be fast to be a good operator. As you can tell, it was all great fun - a real birthday treat.

Started on 20m which was wide open for a short time. Managed to work David VK6KD/4 at Tilpa....but I thought Tilpa was in NSW? Ross was coming into WA S8 for about 20 minutes, then the 20m band died dramatically. I was having a lovely chat with Mark on 80m until a fat finger hit the dummy load button. It appears there are two dummy loads in the shack!
DL3YZ@20, VK2KI@20, VK7TA@20, VK2IOW@20, M0NNK@20, VK3DRQ@20

the 40m band was fairly quiet this week,
until 1800 pm, when the northern QRN started,
the contacts were there, but tricky to work.
For Folks in WA - Don't forget WAs Friday arvo session.
Please disregard my comment in my first report about the VK5, it was a VK2 and not part of our group 👍😊

3 good QSOs with Dylon, Adam and John. Signals faded after an hour or so as the QRM from   radar?, nearby CW and SSB pushed the S5 noise level up and up. A good long QSO with the traveller John VK2RU was a great exchange and will prompt me to update my QRZ page to include the key I use.

40m seemed to be doing ok when I dragged myself away from 20m kicking and screaming at around 0830z.  The band was open to WA with some solid signals my way.  I came across Daniel VK6WE at Cottesloe calling CQ and with fingers on key, was about to say g'day when Mike VK6AAV popped up and called instead.  Great to hear both Daniel and Mike on again and both coming through so well.

A few CQs of my own and I heard what sounded like a strong signal nearby - key clicks and a bit of background noise pumping.  I called again and heard the same;  time to push the pile of paperwork away from my Trio TS-120S to find the RIT button;  the clarifier confirmed that in fact, it was Lance VK7TO calling me - his Kenwood TS-530S was S9 but zero-beat on my carrier frequency.  Last week's SWL challenge was our three-way QSO with James VK3JFR;  this week it was split-frequency operation (it's all part of the plan didn't you know?).  Anyway, we enjoyed our split-frequency rag-chew until it was time for me to be more sociable and help a little dinner-wise.

[20m]
On Sunday on my way back from the chook tractor between bouts of coughing and spluttering, I happened to look up and noticed my very old and fragile 300 Ohm TV ribbon excuse for a feedline hanging loose.  About half way along the 40m suspended run between the house and my 80m double-extended Zepp, the impedance took a jump.  So there's a dilemma for someone with a three-week old cold and lung infection.... get up and fix it, or look away quickly?

Well. the next day I was up there with my soldering iron;  what fun.  One day, one day, I'll replace the old ribbon with some proper home-brewed balanced feeder.... one day!

So now it's Tuesday.... I listened out for Willie DJ9FM at 0600z this week.  Willie was only just audible in the noise here - I couldn't even make out any characters.  However, by 0615, his signal came up a tad, and I was able to make out bits and pieces of his callsign;  I tried calling, but my 50W into a non-gain antenna just wasn't cutting the mustard in Frankfurt (if you catch my drift).  Then to add to the fun, a QRQ station came up smack on Willie's frequency and proceeded to do his thing.  Willie reported via the DL3YZ Runners Point website hearing Lance VK7TO at one stage - but I don't think they caught each-other.

I was giving the new VK1HF Ikara KiwiSDR a go in it's testing configuration at Spring Range, just near the Northern border of the ACT.  Pleased to hear that signals were better on that receiver than here - a good start for the project.  Stay tuned for more as Ian's comms trailer gets set-up with better antennas etc.

I then heard Mike DL3YZ coming through - up and down in the QSB but I was able to give him RSN 311.  Mike then went on to chat to Ian VK7TA at Latrobe;  even though I couldn't hear Ian, it was still good to hear him if you know what I mean!  Ditto for Mike's QSO with Manny - VK3DRQ - not a sausage here.... but Melbourne is in the skip zone for 20m from here - so it would have been unusual to hear him anyway.  Patrick VK2IOW up at Millthrope on the other hand was romping in.

Next Ross reported that he was on air, but 1kHz higher due to QRM from the US.  Really pleased to hear him coming through so nicely this week - RSN 411 from me and he reported RSN 563 for my 50W!  Just in time too  - suddenly my noise level jumped in that distinct-sounding rain static - up at a constant S3.  I had to quickly adjust my T-coupler for maximum output power several times as the rain soaked the rope holding my 300 Ohm feedline.

Around 0800z I heard Carlos CT7BPF very weakly here - I could just hear him in the noise but was not able to pick out characters.  However as Carlos' chat with VK3XU continued, his signals started notching up and I was starting to get the occasional character on QSB peaks before he gave it away for the day.

A fun afternoon on 20m for me this week.

[80m]
After dinner, the KiwiSDRs at Spring Range and Mount Barker didn't look very interesting on 40m - lots of SSB and QRQ - so it was straight to the poolroom 80m for me.  

Georg VK2DLF up at St Marys and Maitland VK5AO at Banksia Park were pouring in, so I found a quiet spot and convinced my T-Match antenna coupler to feed some power into what semblance of a feedline it could.  

That was rewarded by what sounded like an S8 local call - but no, for the second week in a row, the Weinmeister himself Wayne VK6NW was thundering in from Bridgetown.  I'm convinced that Max VK6FN must have loaned one of his filing-cabinet 120 Watt Py amplifiers to Wayne - amazing signals into my slightly sick and poorly-aligned Trio TS-120S.  

So we rolled back and forth with perfect RSN 582 conditions my way, until when I passed it back to Wayne at one stage there was nothing - just noise to be heard.  Assuming a phone-call (Wayne is one of the Bridgetown SES Poohbahs) I waited patiently, then flashed Wayne a WhatsApp note.  

A rather sheepish response came back..... oops two dummies in the shack - he'd selected the dummy load when switching antennas, and was transmitting on that.  Conditions were certainly good - and it's not beyond the realms of possibility that I might hear a bit of stray radiated EM radiation.... but no banana this week!  

So we had a good laugh and carried on until I called stumps;  I'd been fighting a cough / cold / lung-infection for the past three weeks, and it was time to give it a rest.  And besides, Wayne needed to brush the dust off his formal net control hat in preparation for Wednesday's CQQRS Post Morsum net, so with a shave and a haircut, we went our separate ways.

Great fun again this week - thank you one and all.
VK2VCA VK3DBD VK6KHZ VK7TA VK5CZ VK6IS VK6WE VK6AAV
DJ9FM@20 VK2IOW@20 VK6NW@20 CT7BPF@20 VK3XU@20 VK2DLF VK5AO
VK5 using a keyboard at 40wpm - wouldn’t slow down for two others who called them; a major LID!

20m I listened for Willie but did not hear him. There was a Russian station calling on 14037. I heard Mike in QSO with Mark, but could not hear Mark at all. I hope I jumped in at the right time, and just managed a short contact with Mike. I just managed to copy Ross's callsign, but his signal was just too low for me to try and call. 
80m There were some strong ssb signals, so the band seemed to be in reasonable shape, but I didn't hear any cw. I did manage a chat with vk6 which was pleasing.
While there appeared to be much activity on 40m, 80m band was open so I opted for stronger rx signals from my portable location in Tilpa NSW.

From my portable setup across the road from the Tilpa pub NSW, 80m band was working well in all directions.  All those I had a QSO with please correct your logs as no, I'm not in vk4, I'm portable in vk2 at present.  Pretty sure I was incorrectly stating my location as vk4. That was a rookie mistake on my part. It took me 3 days to work out local time in Broken Hill in NSW (they run on SA time) just to move on East and local time jumped again, hihi.  Hope to catch you all next Tue night from a new portable location somewhere in NSW. 73
Excellent signals on 80M, Got to work Ross on 20M nice to be home a bit earlier to catch the DX
VK4BKD, VK5GG, VK5CZ, VK2RU, VK3BSE, VK2KI, VK7TO, VK6KHZ, VK3ACU,

I was away to the West so did not get on air this week. However i went to Bunbury to visit (stir up) VK6FN -Max at Bunbury Hospital. Max must have made a mark at the hospital for when I asked reception where would I find Max, the clerk without refering to her computer, passed me a piece of paper with his ward on it. 

Max and I discussed matters radio and his recent reading of the ARRL Antenna Handbook which was sitting on his chest table. It appears Max has decided it is time to abandon his 360 degree null antenna at last. 

A previous visitor having felt Max may have been a bit confused, I felt duty bound to apply a brief mental state test. I applied the New Zealand short test of cognition which is composed of just three questions - 1. What is the name of the New Zealand rugby team ... answered correctly as the All Blacks.   2. What is required to score a valid try  .... definitely failed that one...   3. What was the score of the last All Blacks game   ..... again a fail. Correct answer is 33/16 in favour of the All Blacks. 

Quite a few in the amateur world have been ringing or visiting Max and clearly that has been appreciated by him.

Donald.

Conditions seemed slightly better than previous weeks on 40 m,  certainly better than last Saturday during the Oceania window for RandomGram.    An observation:  no matter how good the band conditions, they will always be bad for anyone listening to an operator sending at extreme QRS,  around 2 wpm, with inter-character spaces as long as or longer than word spaces.  I'm bemused.  Any idea what such an operator is trying to achieve when he is quite capable of an average 12 wpm QSO, and the stations he works are known by all to be significantly more capable than that.  Why are the brakes being held on so hard and who benefits from such unrealistic sending?  Just asking.

Treated to a dozen or so strong Oceania stations on 80 m working the Sprints, then a successful NZ Net working towards the MWP Traffic badge until 0930Z.    When all had turned to near silence heard very weak VK6TX in QLD, and a QSO where VK3ACU was running 35 watts, so maybe not too bad after all.  Called CQ for 20 minutes, then when about to give up suddenly VK3BWN pops up with a reasonable 442 signal, rounding off the evening very nicely.  TU Ketut.
VK2KI VK6KHZ  VK3TBR  VK6HW  VK7TO  JF1LXO
Beautiful South Bowning via the VK6BL KiwiSDR at Mt Barker.

[20m]
This week I was listening on the KLiwiSDR of Bevan VK6BL at Mount Barker;  thanks Bevan.  However, I was concentrating a bit more on the testing of VK1HF's Ikara KiwiSDR at Spring Range NSW, so not much to report from the West this week.  Nothing at all heard from the DXperiment crew in Europe.

Having recently reconfigured my station, I could once again easily use my TS-530s boat anchor.  It took a little reminding how to tune up the rig's valve finals, but was soon traversing 40 m looking for signals.  

I was fortunate enough to happen across Rob, VK3ECH, a fellow Kenwood aficionado.  He was using his TS-990 and mentioned that he also has a TS-520s, my favourite of the boat anchors, but alas mine lacks a CW filter.

Next up was Mark, VK2KI, with an unexpectedly strong 599+ for the second week in a row.  I should have asked if he's changed his antenna recently; perhaps if I find him next week.  We had a lovely long rag chew, with mark commenting on my wayward signal, finding it hard to zero beat my QSO partners.

My last QRS contact of the evening was a quick report exchange with Paul, VK3KLE.  

Before going QRT for the evening I bumped into VK5GG; a very distinct callsign with his bug accent.  Switching from the straight key to the paddle let me finish the evening with a slightly quicker paced final QSO.
I tried calling CQ on 80, but was getting no takers, and poor reports on the RBN.  It was perhaps a little early in the evening, so hope others were able to enjoy the band later on.
